title: Oncall Incident Starter SDK with Trace Snippet Summarization and Slack Thread Composer
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a lightweight 'Incident Starter SDK' and server-side webhook transformer that creates a compact, contextual incident starter when an SLO/alert fires. The starter includes: a 3‑line human summary, trace snippet (top spans + error overlays), relevant metric spikes (time-windowed), a pointer to the latest logs, and a pre-populated Slack thread starter + PagerDuty event enrichment fields. The feature is intended to reduce on-call time-to-context and to standardize postmortem seeds so that runbooks are easier to author and incidents are triaged faster.

Scope:
- SDK (Go/TS) helpers to attach trace span selectors and sample queries to alerts
- A server-side webhook transformer service that consumes alerts/trace links and emits enriched PagerDuty events and Slack messages
- Slack thread composer templates that encourage fast TTR (triage checklist + suggested owners + initial hypothesis)
- Minimal post-incident artifact linking: auto-create a draft postmortem doc link and attach to the PD incident metadata
- Telemetry for success rate of enrichment, time-to-first-comment and whether the incident starter reduced initial triage time (tracked in the console)

Design decisions / trade-offs considered: 
- Degree of automation: we considered auto-creating postmortems but decided to only attach a draft link to avoid false positives and noisy docs.
- Trace snippet length: balance between useful context vs noise. We limit to 3 spans (root/error span + up to two adjacent causal spans) and a 1200-char summarized stacktrace. This keeps PD/Slack messages compact.
- Where to run summarization: initially run in the webhook transformer (hosted) for speed; design includes an option to push summarization to customer's Dedicated/Private runtime in a later iteration for data residency.
- PagerDuty vs Slack payload shape: PD gets structured fields (service, severity, runbook link, trace_id, top_errors) while Slack gets an expandable thread starter with attachments and an obfuscated trace link for access control.

Ops & Security notes:
- Transformer will redact PII and API keys using the existing redact-regex rules.
- Access to raw trace payloads is limited to RBAC roles (on-call, SRE); we will reuse console RBAC.
- This feature requires a security review because PD metadata can contain sensitive links (security_review_required=true).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal Redwood services only; enable via feature flag and send to a staging PD service + test Slack workspace.
2) Beta: opt-in customers with Dedicated; optional agent that runs summarization in-customer (for data residency).
3) GA: expose as console toggle with per-team templates and retention settings.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK available (Go + TypeScript) with examples in the repo and automated integration tests.
- Webhook transformer successfully enriches 95% of test alerts in staging with trace snippets and metrics summary.
- Slack thread template created and visible in a staging workspace.
- PagerDuty events receive structured enrichment fields and PD incidents display the draft postmortem link.
- Console telemetry surfaces: enrichment success rate, average enrichment latency (< 1s added), and reduction in median time-to-first-comment for pilot teams (target: 15% improvement).

Files & artifacts: see links below for the design doc, initial spec, and the prototype PR.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Observability, and PM. Agreed on scope for alpha: internal services only, limited to traces/metrics (no logs full-text).
2026-03-04: PoC for trace summarization completed (Python prototype). Prototype selects root error span + two causal spans and produces a 900-char summary. Sharing results in #obs-infra.
2026-03-06: Implemented initial Go SDK helpers and added an example alert rule in staging. Raised PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4523.
2026-03-08: Design review with Security attended. Decided to run redaction in transformer and to mark PD metadata as confidential. Security asked for an audit log entry for each enrichment action.

2026-03-10: End-to-end test in staging succeeded for PD enrichment and Slack thread compose. Measuring telemetry instrumentation (added metrics: enrichment_success, enrichment_latency_ms, starter_created).
comments: Lucia Morales (SRE): Verify that the transformer doesn't elevate permissions for runtime access to traces; prefer generating expiry-limited pre-signed trace links.
Priya Rao (PM): Add an optional 'initial-owner' suggestion using recent deploy owners or service owners if available in Service Catalog.
Jordan Kim (Design): Slack thread starter should have a collapsible checklist and a CTA to 'Create Postmortem' which opens the draft with prefilled fields.
Security (review note): Must log the redaction decision and store a redaction_diff for audits. Ensure retention policy aligns with customer settings.
Arjun Patel (assignee): Will follow up with a small migration plan for existing alert transformers and schedule a runbook session with SRE next week.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Go/TS) with examples and CI coverage
Transformer enriches PD + Slack messages with trace snippet, metric spike summary, and draft postmortem link
Console displays enrichment telemetry and shows per-team enable/disable toggle
Security review completed and audit logs created for each enrichment event
Internal pilot demonstrates >=15% reduction in time-to-first-comment for engaged teams
notes: Try to keep Slack messages compact: use attachments and collapsible blocks. For PD, use structured metadata fields so downstream tools (runbooks, crawl bots) can discover incident seeds. Consider a future integration to auto-suggest likely RCA owners using code-owner mappings and recent deploys.
